findings.title: Task 22a's wall-clock bound has a thin margin over the single local measurement
findings.description: Description: `MAX_LISTING_S = 1.0` is asserted over "a few hundred" seeded files, but the only measurement behind it is the design's "0.67 s for 188 runs", presumably local; that is a ~1.5x margin, and the load test now gates CI (`uv run pytest` on ubuntu-latest runners, plus the hermetic job). The repo's load-test precedent (`test_usage_reader_loop.py`) deliberately uses bounds generous to CI jitter. Nothing to change before starting — the test will reveal the real CI cost at Task 22a — but if it proves flaky on CI, the fix is to lower the seed count for CI or widen the constant with a recorded rationale, not to remove the assertion.

findings.title: Task 42 runs walkthrough step 8 under a scratch HOME, not the design's "real runs dir"
findings.description: Description: The design's walkthrough step 8 measures `sq runs list --all` against the real runs directory (188 runs); Task 42 runs it in the scratch HOME seeded with ~5 runs. This is a legitimate refinement — the design marks the walkthrough "Draft, to be refined in Phase 6", and the actual few-hundred-files cost measurement is enforced by Task 22a — but it means the walkthrough step only smoke-checks the listing path; the real assertion lives in the load test. No action required; recorded so the deviation is a conscious one.
